accuracy.claim: No dependencies beyond runtime built-ins (node:http, node:test, node:assert/strict, global fetch and URL); no dependency list, lockfile or install step; why stated at README.md:3
accuracy.note: package.json has no dependency keys; README.md:3 says 'no dependencies' and the description says 'dependency-free'; only node:-prefixed built-ins are required; no lockfile is tracked or present.

accuracy.claim: Source and test files are CommonJS in strict mode, each ending with one module.exports object naming its public functions; built-ins required with the node: prefix
accuracy.note: Wrong detail: the four test files have no module.exports at all (grep count 0); only the four src files end with one. CommonJS (package.json type), 'use strict' first in all eight files and node:-prefixed built-ins all hold.

accuracy.claim: Routing is hand-written in the one listener createServer builds: request target to URL, branch on method and path, exact comparison for the list, anchored pattern for one user, ending in not-found
accuracy.note: src/server.js: new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost'); url.pathname === '/users'; /^\/users\/(\d+)$/; final send(res, 404, { error: 'not found' }). README.md:8 names node:http.

accuracy.claim: Every answer goes through send, which sets only the JSON content type and writes compact JSON; an error answer is an object with a single error property holding a constant text
accuracy.note: send calls writeHead(status, { 'content-type': 'application/json' }) and end(JSON.stringify(body)) with no spacing; all three answers use it; the only error body is the literal { error: 'not found' }.

accuracy.claim: Failures reach HTTP callers only as the 404 not-found answer; helpers throw TypeError/RangeError; the listener has no try/catch so a thrown error never becomes a JSON answer
accuracy.note: No try, catch or process handler in any tracked file (grep); paginate and truncate/capitalize throw TypeError/RangeError; the code's only error answer is 404.

accuracy.claim: State is a module-level constant array read only through getUser (stored record) and listUsers (new list of the same records); the server never touches the array and nothing writes it
accuracy.note: const USERS in src/users.js; getUser returns USERS.find(...), listUsers returns USERS.slice(); USERS is not exported and has no writers; README.md:7 'an in-memory user store'.

accuracy.claim: The only setting, PORT, is read once inside the require.main block with fallback 3000; modules read no environment when loaded; createServer takes no options
accuracy.note: The only process.env read is src/server.js line 26, inside if (require.main === module): Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000; createServer() has no parameters.

accuracy.claim: createServer returns a non-listening server; tests listen on an ephemeral 127.0.0.1 port, use global fetch, close in finally, mock nothing; why stated in the createServer comment
accuracy.note: Doc comment: 'not listening until the caller calls listen()'; withServer calls server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1') and closes the server in a finally block; nothing is mocked.

accuracy.claim: Built-in runner with strict assertions; one test file per source module named after it; test command is the runner's own discovery with no configuration; sentence test names
accuracy.note: node:test and node:assert/strict; server/users/paginate/strings each have a matching <name>.test.js; scripts.test is the bare 'node --test'; README.md:10.

accuracy.claim: Requests are answered synchronously from memory; no timers, queues, workers or shutdown hooks
accuracy.note: The listener is synchronous; no setTimeout/setInterval/Worker/cluster/process.on anywhere (grep).

accuracy.claim: No identity or access layer: the listener looks only at method and path, treats every caller alike, returns stored records whole including email
accuracy.note: The listener reads only req.method and req.url; there is no auth of any kind; send serialises whole USERS records, email included.

accuracy.claim: Helper modules are pure, argument-checking and stand alone; only their tests call the paging and text helpers; paginate reports page, page count and items but not length or size
accuracy.note: Only test/paginate.test.js and test/strings.test.js require src/paginate and src/strings (grep); paginate returns { page, pages, items }.

accuracy.claim: GET /users answers 200 with a JSON array of every user in ascending id order, today ids 1, 2 and 3
accuracy.note: server.js: GET && pathname === '/users' -> send(res, 200, listUsers()); listUsers returns USERS.slice() in stored order 1, 2, 3.

accuracy.claim: GET /users/:id with id one or more decimal digits and nothing after answers 200 with that user's object when the user exists
accuracy.note: The anchored pattern /^\/users\/(\d+)$/ (ASCII digits, no u flag) feeds getUser(Number(id)); the cited test asserts /users/1 gives 200 and 'Ada Lovelace'. The digit-pattern detail comes from createServer, which the entry's Source line also cites.

accuracy.claim: Every answer is compact JSON with content-type: application/json, no charset, and the code sets no other header
accuracy.note: send sets one header and JSON.stringify(body) without indentation; Node's automatic headers are not set by the code, as the bullet says.

accuracy.note: Matches the USERS literal in src/users.js.

accuracy.claim: Paging inputs are a list, a 1-based page number and a page size; no defaults; an omitted one is invalid
accuracy.note: paginate(items, page, size) has no defaults; undefined fails Array.isArray or Number.isInteger and throws; start = (page - 1) * size.

accuracy.claim: The start command serves on PORT; unset, empty, 0 or non-numeric PORT gives 3000
accuracy.note: scripts.start = 'node src/server.js'; Number(PORT) || 3000. In Node, Number(undefined), Number(''), Number('0') and Number('x') all fall back to 3000.

accuracy.claim: Nothing runs apart from answering requests: no timers, queues, workers, watchers, start-up tasks or scheduled jobs; each request is answered from memory
accuracy.note: No such constructs in any tracked file (grep); the listener reads the in-memory array synchronously.

accuracy.claim: No credential is asked for or checked; any caller that reaches the port may use every route
accuracy.note: The listener inspects only method and URL; there are no headers, cookies or auth logic.

accuracy.claim: Every answer carrying a user carries all its properties, email included, with no field selection, masking or per-caller filtering
accuracy.note: Both success paths pass the stored record(s) straight to send/JSON.stringify.

accuracy.claim: The test command runs the built-in runner with no file list; the baseline run found the seven existing tests in four files under test
accuracy.note: scripts.test = 'node --test' with no paths; tests per file: server 1, users 2, paginate 2, strings 2, so 7 in 4 files (counted from source; per the judging rules the run itself was not repeated).

accuracy.claim: The query string is never read: any query parameter leaves the answer unchanged; only method and path pick the route
accuracy.note: Only url.pathname is used; there is no searchParams/search read (grep); new URL('/users?page=1').pathname is '/users'. Outside the sample: R-1 b4's 'only the exact path /users' is slightly loose, because the comparison is on the normalised pathname, so /a/../users also gets the listing.

accuracy.claim: Inferred, not run: an error raised while handling a request is not caught, gives no JSON error and as an unhandled exception would stop the process, e.g. a request target the URL parser rejects
accuracy.note: There is no try/catch, and new URL('//', 'http://localhost') throws ERR_INVALID_URL (checked with a node one-liner that runs no repository code). A synchronous throw in a request listener is an uncaught exception, which ends the process by default. It is correctly labelled inferred.

accuracy.claim: Each listing is a new list, so reordering it leaves the store alone, but its users and the user a lookup returns are the stored records, so changing one changes the store
accuracy.note: USERS.slice() is a shallow copy; getUser returns the element found by USERS.find; the records are not frozen.

accuracy.claim: The page count is length / size rounded down, so a trailing partial page is never counted or returned: 7 entries at size 3 give pages 2 and entry 7 is unreachable
accuracy.note: pages = Math.floor(items.length / size), and items are returned only when page <= pages; floor(7/3) = 2, so page 3 returns [].

accuracy.claim: Invalid input throws in order list (TypeError), size, then page (RangeError, 'must be a positive integer'); size error wins; no upper limit; numeric text invalid; only size 0 tested
accuracy.note: The check order and messages match src/paginate.js; there is no upper bound; Number.isInteger('2') is false; the only invalid-input test is paginate([1], 1, 0).

coverage.note: R-1 b1-b3 cover the 200 array of id/name/email in id order with the query ignored; R-1 b5 says no HTTP test exists and the store test only counts 3; R-4 b3 adds that the count is pinned.
R-2 b1/b2/b4 cover digits giving 200 or 404 and a non-digit id giving 404; R-3 b2 gives the {error} body. The literal text 'not found' appears only in prose ('the one error in use is not found').
R-3 b3 covers every other method or path giving the same 404; R-3 b1 and AD-4 cover the JSON body with content-type application/json.
R-6 b1 covers PORT with default 3000 via the start command; R-6 b4 and AD-7/AD-8 say loading never listens and the require.main block alone reads PORT.

R-5 covers 1-based paging (b1), validation (b7), the floor page count that drops a partial last page (b4, b5, including the request's own case of 3 users at size 10 giving 0 pages), the evenly-divided-only test (b3, R-10 b6) and the conflict with README.md:6 (b10, Source conflict).
No dependencies, CommonJS strict mode, {error} JSON errors, in-memory array, built-in node:test run by npm test (named in Stack).

examples: R-3 b5: 'as an unhandled exception ... a request target the URL parser rejects' (exception mechanism, URL parser)
R-5 b7: 'rejected by throwing ... a type error ... a range error ... only real numbers pass' (language exception types; the in-process helper's contract)
R-5 b9: 'the server's only local import is the user store' (module import graph)
R-9 b4: 'the id is limited to digits by an anchored pattern' (regex mechanism)
R-10 b7: 'Paging with a size of 0 is rejected as a range error' (language exception type)
R-10 b8: 'a maximum of 0 is rejected as a range error' (language exception type)
borderline_not_counted: Spec: R-4 b2 'or null'; R-5 b2 and R-10 b6 'strict deep equality'; R-10 b1 'the platform's built-in runner' (refers to the runner without naming it)

Architecture: AD-5's first sentence and AD-11's 'treats every caller alike and returns stored user records whole, email included' restate R-3 b2 and R-9 b1, but each entry's subject is structural (no catch; no access layer), so neither is counted

R-1 documented (README.md:8): the line says only that the server 'serves the users' and documents no route (the spec's Overview says so itself); it supports the purpose, not the GET /users contract. Weak, not wrong.

summary: Reliable: 26 of 27 sampled claims hold against the code with no miscitations, including every request-critical fact (GET /users answers the whole array in id order and never reads the query, every other request gets the JSON {error} 404, PORT is read only when server.js is the entry, and paginate's floor page count drops a partial last page, worked through the request's own case of 3 users at size 10 giving 0 pages), and every Source label fits its evidence. Wrong: nothing is outright wrong; AD-2 is partial because it says test files also end with a module.exports object, which only the four source files do. Missing: all six expected facts are present, so nothing material is missing; the weakness is leakage, with six requirement bullets using implementation vocabulary (thrown type/range errors, the URL parser, the import graph, the anchored id pattern), mostly where the spec describes the in-process helpers' contracts.
